explanations.explanation: You got it, baker! David says, "I shall not want" in Psalm 23:1. That means with the LORD looking out for him, he won't lack a single thing he actually needs.
Not quite, friend. David isn't talking about working for his keep here. He says, "I shall not want," meaning he won't lack what he needs because the Shepherd provides it all (Psalm 23:1).
That's not what David says. He opens with, "I shall not want" in Psalm 23:1. He's focusing on how he won't lack anything under the Shepherd's care, not whether he'll lose things.
Baked just right, baker! Green pastures for lying down and quiet waters for drinking (Psalm 23:2) are all about deep, undisturbed rest. It's the ultimate picture of peace.
No hustle in these pastures, friend! Lying down in green grass and walking by quiet, still waters (Psalm 23:2) is a picture of complete rest, not a busy workday.
Actually, it's the exact opposite! Quiet waters and green pastures (Psalm 23:2) show a place of absolute safety and calm, far away from any panic or danger.
That's a keeper! Psalm 23:3 says, "He restores my soul." When life gets heavy and wears you down to a nub, the Shepherd brings you back to life and refills your tank.
Not this time, friend. While there are times of testing in life, David says right here that the LORD "restores my soul" (Psalm 23:3). It's all about healing and renewal.
Not quite. David isn't talking about being measured or evaluated here. He says the LORD "restores my soul" (Psalm 23:3), bringing refreshing and healing to his inner life.

explanations.answer: For the sake of His name
explanations.explanation: Perfect bake! Psalm 23:3 says He guides us in righteous paths "for the sake of His name." The Shepherd's own reputation is on the line, so you know He's going to lead us the right way.

explanations.answer: For the sake of His flock
explanations.explanation: Though the flock certainly benefits from the right paths, David says the LORD guides him "for the sake of His name" (Psalm 23:3). It's about showing who He is through His faithful leading.

explanations.answer: For the sake of His land
explanations.explanation: The land isn't the reason here. David says the Shepherd guides him in paths of righteousness "for the sake of His name" (Psalm 23:3). His leading reflects His own perfect character.

explanations.answer: Because the LORD is with him
explanations.explanation: Box-worthy! David says, "I will fear no evil, for You are with me" (Psalm 23:4). The dark doesn't get any less dark, but having the Shepherd right next to you changes everything.
No, David isn't relying on his own muscles here. He says he fears no evil "for You are with me" (Psalm 23:4). His confidence comes entirely from the Shepherd's presence, not his own strength.
Actually, David doesn't say how long the valley is. He can face even a long, terrifying walk because "You are with me" (Psalm 23:4), no matter how long the shadows stretch.

You got it, baker! Psalm 23:4 says, "Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me." In a dark place, knowing the Shepherd has the tools to protect you and pull you out of trouble is incredibly comforting.
Actually, it is true! Even though a rod and staff are heavy tools, David says, "Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me" (Psalm 23:4). They show him the Shepherd is ready to protect and rescue him.
Fine work, baker! Psalm 23:5 says, "You prepare a table before me." The Shepherd becomes a generous host, laying out a feast to honor His guest.
Not quite a tent, friend. David says the LORD prepares a "table" before him (Psalm 23:5). It's a beautiful picture of being invited to sit down for a grand, peaceful meal.
Not a bed this time. David says the LORD prepares a "table" before him (Psalm 23:5). The focus here is on a rich feast prepared by a loving host.

Actually, it is false! Psalm 23:5 says the table is prepared "in the presence of my enemies." The enemies have to sit there and watch the LORD honor and feed David, which is a massive statement of safety.

That's a keeper! The table is prepared "in the presence of my enemies" (Psalm 23:5). David doesn't have to wait for his troubles to disappear to enjoy the feast; the LORD feeds him right in front of them.
Baked just right! An overflowing cup (Psalm 23:5) means the host doesn't just fill it to the brim; He keeps pouring. It's a picture of God's abundant, non-stop generosity.
No carelessness here! An overflowing cup (Psalm 23:5) isn't a messy accident. It's a picture of the host being so incredibly generous that the cup can't even hold all the goodness.
Nobody is rushing David at this table! The overflowing cup (Psalm 23:5) is a picture of luxury and abundance, showing he has absolutely all the time and resources he could ever want.
Perfect bake! Psalm 23:6 says, "Surely goodness and mercy will follow me all the days of my life." Instead of enemies chasing him down, David has God's own love and kindness hot on his heels.
Though David was a king, he doesn't mention money or fame here. He says "goodness and mercy" will follow him all his days (Psalm 23:6). Those are the real treasures.
Those are great things, but David's song points to something else. He says "goodness and mercy" will follow him all the days of his life (Psalm 23:6), chasing him down wherever he goes.

explanations.answer: In the house of the LORD
explanations.explanation: Box-worthy! David closes the psalm by saying, "and I will dwell in the house of the LORD forever" (Psalm 23:6). It's the ultimate happy ending: going home to stay with the Host forever.
Hebron was an important city in David's life, but his song looks far beyond any earthly kingdom. He says he will dwell "in the house of the LORD forever" (Psalm 23:6).
Not Canaan. David's final destination in this beautiful song is much closer to home for his soul. He says, "I will dwell in the house of the LORD forever" (Psalm 23:6).
